summary: A [five-year technology authority strategic plan](2026-06-22-nita-u-five-year-digital-strategy) was launched in June 2026, and the plan document is not held.
developments:
The plan covers financial years 2025/26 to 2029/30 and was launched in the capital ([plan](2026-06-22-nita-u-five-year-digital-strategy)).

Its one figure that reaches this report is an agency-integration baseline for the government data exchange, recorded separately.

A five-year plan whose text is unavailable is the frame for a unit that otherwise reports a great deal: 143 sourced rows, and the governing strategy is not among them.

summary: A [National AI and Emerging Technologies Strategy](2026-08-04-ministry-reviews-5-year-performance-on-ugandas-digital-transformation-journey) holds the same status at both ends of the window, while an [AI secretariat](2026-03-12-govt-crafts-national-ai-strategy) operates with no budget line or mandate document held.
developments:
The strategy was reported in development in June 2025 and again in August 2026 as due by the financial year's end; the same status at both ends of the window is the finding ([strategy](2026-08-04-ministry-reviews-5-year-performance-on-ugandas-digital-transformation-journey), [outlook](2026-07-30-cipit-east-african-ai-policy-outlook-report), [crafting](2026-03-12-govt-crafts-national-ai-strategy), [policy](2025-06-18-uganda-to-develop-national-ai-policy), [rights](2026-05-11 CIPESA Urges Rights-Centred Approach to Uganda’s AI Strategy)).

A ministry secretariat is reported operating under a named head with no budget line, staffing figure or mandate document held ([secretariat](2026-03-12-govt-crafts-national-ai-strategy)).

A separate policy to regulate artificial intelligence and social media was announced to an editors' guild meeting; it is distinct from the strategy and the base holds no other record of it ([media policy](2026-08-02-editors-raise-alarm-over-ai-misuse-journalist-identity-data-protection-gaps)).

progress: Mixed, five Computer Misuse Act sections nullified for vagueness while vandalism enforcement was stepped up as economic sabotage
summary: The Constitutional Court [nullified five sections of the Computer Misuse Act](2026-03-17-constitutional-court-nullifies-computer-misuse-act) on quorum and vagueness grounds, and government [declared telecom-infrastructure attacks economic sabotage](2026-07-31-government-declares-telecom-infrastructure-vandalism-economic-sabotage).
developments:
The nullification covered sections 11, 23 and 26 to 29. The movement stem records an instrument neutralised; the rights reading is the opposite ([nullification](2026-03-17-constitutional-court-nullifies-computer-misuse-act)).

Vandalism against telecommunications infrastructure is now treated as economic sabotage, with a subscriber-card conviction obtained under the 2024 interception regulations rather than the Act ([sabotage](2026-07-31-government-declares-telecom-infrastructure-vandalism-economic-sabotage), [crackdown](2026-07-23-uganda-crackdown-telecoms-vandalism)).

Which statute an offence is charged under is worth recording when the principal computer-crime Act has just lost five sections.

summary: A [Protection of Sovereignty Bill](2026-04-30-bou-governor-warns-protection-of-sovereignty-bill) caps foreign funding at about UGX 400m a year above which ministerial approval is required, and the regulator [opened nationwide enforcement against unlicensed public wireless access](2026-07-08-ucc-enforcement-against-illegal-public-wifi).
developments:
The bill was assessed technically by the central bank to joint committees in April 2026; enactment is reported but unconfirmed ([bill](2026-04-30-bou-governor-warns-protection-of-sovereignty-bill), [editors](2026-08-02-editors-raise-alarm-over-ai-misuse-journalist-identity-data-protection-gaps)).

A cap on foreign funding with ministerial approval above it reaches every civil-society body in this ledger — the digital-rights submissions, the awareness campaigns and the climate-information project are all externally funded.

Nationwide enforcement against unlicensed public wireless access opened on a public notice in July 2026 ([enforcement](2026-07-08-ucc-enforcement-against-illegal-public-wifi)).

summary: [Digital lending platform regulation](2026-08-18-monitor-uganda-digital-lender-regulation) was stated as intended at a finance ministry and parliamentary retreat, with no bill, instrument or timetable held.
developments:
The intention was stated in August 2026 ([intention](2026-08-18-monitor-uganda-digital-lender-regulation)).

It is the only payments-specific legislative movement in this ledger, against a payments record that includes a stablecoin corridor, a tokenised-asset exchange, a currency-settlement service and a credit-scoring memorandum with nothing published about its consent or legal basis.

summary: The [Data Protection and Privacy Act](2026-08-19-monitor-pdpo-35000-unregistered-data-controllers) is in force and the office's director stated a shortfall of some 35,000 unregistered controllers against a 50,000 estimate.
developments:
The statute did not change; the estimate is the office's own and no prosecution outcome is held ([shortfall](2026-08-19-monitor-pdpo-35000-unregistered-data-controllers), [enforcement](2026-07-29-whatsapp-privacy-updates-uganda-data-protection-enforcement), [decision](2026-02-20-uganda-pdpo-decision-adlegal-v-whatsapp-meta), [order](2025-07-18-uganda-pdpo-ssekamwa-frank-v-google-llc-decision)).

Registration at roughly three parts in ten of the office's own estimate of the controller population, three years into the regime, is what the enforcement record below has to be read against.

summary: The protection office [confirmed compliance by a global messaging platform](2026-07-29-whatsapp-privacy-updates-uganda-data-protection-enforcement) in July 2026, and its [earlier orders against a search company](2025-07-18-uganda-pdpo-ssekamwa-frank-v-google-llc-decision) have no recorded compliance step.
developments:
The messaging decision was made in February 2026 and compliance confirmed by a letter of July 2026, which is correspondence and is not held ([compliance](2026-07-29-whatsapp-privacy-updates-uganda-data-protection-enforcement), [decision](2026-02-20-uganda-pdpo-decision-adlegal-v-whatsapp-meta)).

The orders against the search company were decided in July 2025 with thirty days to register and file cross-border evidence; the precedent travelled and the compliance step was never recorded ([orders](2025-07-18-uganda-pdpo-ssekamwa-frank-v-google-llc-decision), [breach](2025-07-20-pdpo-google-breach-cross-border-data)).

A six-month awareness campaign launched in December 2025 targeted reaching 70 per cent of the population and registering 1,000 controllers ([campaign](2025-12-11-vuka-africa-prosecuted-data-breach-pdpo)). Two decisions against global platforms, one confirmed and one unrecorded, is the enforcement record.

summary: The revenue authority issued [more than 1,000 compliance notices for bank customer information](2026-08-17-theeastafrican-ura-demand-notices-bank-customer-information) since June 2026, and an editorial argues the [identity number is handed over on request](2026-08-26-uganda-nin-data-protection-observer-editorial) to security guards and others with no lawful basis.
developments:
The demands are made under the tax procedures statute and are set by the paper against the data-protection Act; the revenue authority was unavailable for comment and no determination by the protection office is held ([notices](2026-08-17-theeastafrican-ura-demand-notices-bank-customer-information)).

Public grasp of data-protection principles was cited at an awareness-campaign launch, and an editorial states the identity-number problem as a lived one rather than a survey finding ([grasp](2025-12-11-vuka-africa-prosecuted-data-breach-pdpo), [editorial](2026-08-26-uganda-nin-data-protection-observer-editorial)).

A three-year child online-safety campaign was launched in August 2026 ([children](2026-08-14-uganda-be-a-cyber-hero-campaign-minors)).

summary: A [regulator order suspended public internet](2026-01-13-ucc-directive-suspension-of-internet-services) around the January 2026 election, with [social media still blocked](2026-01-18-govt-restores-partial-internet-social-media-blocked) a week after general restoration.
developments:
A duration must name its endpoint: four days measures order to measured restoration of connectivity, almost five days measures order to the regulator's announced restoration at midnight on 18 January, and thirteen days measures order to full restoration including social media. The directive is held as a scanned document with no text layer, and no ruling in the Law Society suit is on file ([order](2026-01-13-ucc-directive-suspension-of-internet-services), [restoration](2026-01-26-ucc-public-notice-full-restoration-of-internet-services), [record](2026-08-09-isoc-pulse-uganda-january-2026-shutdown-record), [directives](2026-03-10-govt-ordered-table-directives-pre-election-shutdown)).

Social media and over-the-top services remained blocked after general internet was restored ([block](2026-01-18-govt-restores-partial-internet-social-media-blocked), [signal](2025-12-05-govt-signals-social-media-clampdown-elections)).

Revised judiciary media guidelines were issued through the case-management system for a High Court trial; the guidelines themselves are not on file ([guidelines](2026-07-30-uganda-uls-slams-court-restrictions-besigye-treason-trial-eccmis)).

summary: A [joint civil-society submission](2026-07-01-cipesa-apc-wougnet-uganda-fourth-cycle-upr-submission) was filed for the fourth-cycle periodic review, and a [climate information integrity project](2026-08-19-cipesa-unesco-climate-information-integrity) launched in August 2026.
developments:
The submission carries civil-society recommendations rather than government commitments; it carries no day on its cover and the date is padded to the month ([submission](2026-07-01-cipesa-apc-wougnet-uganda-fourth-cycle-upr-submission), [review](2026-08-05-uganda-and-zimbabwes-fourth-cycle-uprs-must-turn-digital-progress-into-stronger-rights-protections)).

The climate project was launched in August 2026 with no budget or duration stated ([project](2026-08-19-cipesa-unesco-climate-information-integrity)).

Both are externally funded, which is why the foreign-funding cap in the sovereignty bill recorded separately bears on whether either continues.

summary: The country [won a four-year seat on a continental telecommunications council](2026-07-26-uganda-wins-seat-african-telecommunications-union-administrative-council), and a [harmonised regional framework for artificial intelligence and digital finance](2026-07-31-eac-central-bankers-single-currency-2031) was proposed and left out of the signed communique.
developments:
The seat was won in July 2026 for a four-year term; the council coordinates African positions on spectrum, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and data governance before the international union ([seat](2026-07-26-uganda-wins-seat-african-telecommunications-union-administrative-council), [declaration](2026-07-27-atu-cpl26-abuja-declaration-sg-election-full-record)).

The harmonised framework was proposed by a monetary affairs committee chair in the capital and is absent from the signed communique; the stated argument for acting regionally is regulatory arbitrage ([framework](2026-07-31-eac-central-bankers-single-currency-2031), [bloc](2026-03-31 EAC moves to create unified AI Sovereignty bloc)).

A regional artificial-intelligence policy roadmap was explored at a science conference with the country a participant rather than a sponsor ([roadmap](2026-03-31 EAC moves to create unified AI Sovereignty bloc)).

summary: A [data sharing agreement under the health memorandum](2026-06-08-hrw-human-rights-assessment-afghs-bilateral-health-agreements) is provided for and still to be executed, alongside a specimen agreement covering genetic sequence data of high-consequence pathogens.
developments:
The agreement is provided for at a numbered clause and is not on record as completed; a specimen sharing agreement covering genetic sequence data during an outbreak is likewise provided for, effective for no more than five years, and is likewise incomplete ([agreement](2026-06-08-hrw-human-rights-assessment-afghs-bilateral-health-agreements), [memorandum](2025-12-10-afghs-mou-uganda), [complaint](2026-04-02-public-citizen-v-department-of-state-foia-complaint)).

The country has a data-protection statute in force and a protection office issuing orders against global platforms, and neither is named in the arrangement.

summary: A [renewed enterprise architecture and interoperability framework](2026-05-27-ega-uganda-renewed-digital-government-frameworks) was delivered in May 2026, and the [government data exchange](2026-06-22-nita-u-five-year-digital-strategy) sits at a 37 per cent agency-integration baseline.
developments:
Neither renewed document is held, and the rollout is not reported ([framework](2026-05-27-ega-uganda-renewed-digital-government-frameworks), [renewal](2026-02-18-ega-uganda-launches-renewal-gea-egif)).

The exchange's integration baseline comes from the authority's five-year strategy; two figures for it use different denominators and are not reconciled ([exchange](2026-06-22-nita-u-five-year-digital-strategy), [case study](2024-06-28 Integrated National Data Exchange Systems - Uganda Case Study)).

The single sign-on service is described in an undated agency deck, proxy-dated at ingest, so its figures must not be read as current ([sign-on](2024-05-21 A Collaborative Approach to Digital Identity and Digital Transformation (NIRA and NITA-U))).

summary: A [US$200m digital acceleration project](2021-06-02-wb-uga-001-uganda-digital-acceleration-project---govnet) running 2021 to 2027 funds three service-centre pilots and the information security framework, and no disbursement figure is held.
developments:
It is named as the funder of the service-centre pilots and of the 2026 information security framework ([project](2021-06-02-wb-uga-001-uganda-digital-acceleration-project---govnet), [pilots](2026-07-27-uganda-tororo-one-stop-service-uganda-centre-inspection), [future](2026-07-24-uganda-beyond-connectivity-building-ugandas-digital-future)).

A distance-education grant of US$12.2m runs 2025 to 2030 for electronic content across 2,560 courses at ten colleges ([education](2025-01-01-koica-uga-makerere-elearning-2025-project-to-enhance-distance-education-environment)).

One lender operation with no disbursement figure carrying the service centres, the security framework and the government network is the shape of external financing here.

summary: [Cooperation talks](2026-08-13-uganda-ethio-telecom-digital-partnership-talks) were held with a neighbouring state operator, with no scope, value or timetable stated.
developments:
A delegation visited in August 2026 ([talks](2026-08-13-uganda-ethio-telecom-digital-partnership-talks)).

Talks only. It is the sole bilateral commercial engagement in this ledger that is not with a Chinese, Gulf or European counterparty, each of which is recorded separately.

summary: [Active mobile subscriptions](2026-07-02-uganda-outlines-next-ict-goals-ucc-stats) and [smartphones in use](2026-07-02-uganda-outlines-next-ict-goals-ucc-stats) both rose on regulator statements, and the regulator states its figures come from licensees' own submissions.
developments:
The subscription figure was stated in July 2026, and the regulator states the figures come from licensees' own submissions ([subscriptions](2026-07-02-uganda-outlines-next-ict-goals-ucc-stats), [report](2025-11-17-ucc-market-performance-report-q3-2025), [submission](2026-07-01-cipesa-apc-wougnet-uganda-fourth-cycle-upr-submission)).

The smartphone figure's start carries no date ([smartphones](2026-07-02-uganda-outlines-next-ict-goals-ucc-stats)).

The leading operator's coverage and fibre footprint come from its own unaudited half-year results, with the base holding no position at the window's opening ([operator](2026-08-07-mtn-group-opcos-deliver-double-digit-growth), [sustainability](2026-08-05-mtn-uganda-sustainability-report-2025)). Every connectivity figure in this unit originates with an operator.

summary: A [device-tax paper was stated ready for cabinet](2026-08-05-uganda-ict-ministry-smartphone-tax-affordability), and [average monthly consumer data spend rose](2026-08-18-ceo-uganda-ucc-q2-2026-market-performance-data-spend) on volumes that moved the implied per-gigabyte cost the other way.
developments:
The regulator proposed major telecom tax cuts and a device-tax paper was stated ready for cabinet in August 2026; the study itself is not held ([paper](2026-08-05-uganda-ict-ministry-smartphone-tax-affordability), [cuts](2026-06-22-ucc-proposes-major-telecom-tax-cuts)).

The two ends of the spend series are on different consumption volumes, so the implied per-gigabyte cost moved the other way; the reporting outlet's own per-gigabyte derivation is not the regulator's figure ([spend](2026-08-18-ceo-uganda-ucc-q2-2026-market-performance-data-spend)).

A regional dataset states a mobile data price printed in dollars with no exchange-rate or conversion basis ([price](2026-08-03-eaco-regional-communications-sector-statistics-report-2025)), and buy-now-pay-later device financing is reported by a trade analysis with no default, repossession or total-cost-of-credit figure published ([financing](2026-08-17-uganda-device-financing-smartphone-penetration)).

summary: Parliament approved an [RMB 1.05bn loan for backbone phase five](2023-12-06-uganda-parliament-hansard-nbi-egi-phase-v-loan) in December 2023, with no newer figure, and service-centre throughput was made contingent on it.
developments:
The loan approval is the last figure on file for the backbone programme ([loan](2023-12-06-uganda-parliament-hansard-nbi-egi-phase-v-loan)).

Making the service centres' throughput contingent on a backbone phase whose latest reported position is a 2023 loan approval is the dependency worth stating.

A 260 km commercial route carrying over 1 Tbit/s was lit before the window opened ([route](2025-05-06-kampala-malaba-fibre-route-bayobab)), and a gigabit fixed broadband product launched in May 2026 with no subscriber, price or footprint figure published ([product](2026-05-04-savanna-fibre-uganda-1gbps-broadband)).

summary: A [2,000 km protected route to the coast](2026-02-09-paratus-goma-mombasa-g2m-fibre-route) was switched on in February 2026, and a [second route to the same coast](2026-06-17 Seacom deploys a new high-capacity Nairobi–Kampala route to strengthen East Africa's digital backbone) launched with 1 Tbps activated.
developments:
The first route was switched on in February 2026 ([route](2026-02-09-paratus-goma-mombasa-g2m-fibre-route), [highway](2026-02-09-paratus-goma-mombasa-fibre-highway-itweb)).

The second launched in June 2026 with 1 Tbps activated, and is absent from the compiled intersection page ([second](2026-06-17 Seacom deploys a new high-capacity Nairobi–Kampala route to strengthen East Africa's digital backbone)).

Two protected routes to the coast inside five months is the most substantive infrastructure gain in this unit, and both are commercial builds with no state instrument attached.

summary: [Commercial service began on 2 September 2026](2026-09-02-newvision-starlink-launch-uganda) under a five-year licence requiring a national gateway, a point of presence and registration of every device activated in the country.
developments:
The licence text is not held; a January 2026 wholesale-model ruling and a May 2026 direct licence are unreconciled, and no subscriber or tariff figure is published ([switch-on](2026-08-22-redpepper-starlink-uganda-roke-paratus), [licence](2026-05-15-starlink-enters-uganda-state-house-license), [wholesale](2026-01-10-uganda-ucc-starlink-wholesale-model), [blocking](2026-01-06-starlink-accepts-uganda-request-block-illegal-users), [shutdown](2026-01-05-uganda-starlink-shutdown-devtelecoms)).

One domestic provider was first in the country to launch the service; it is a reseller launch rather than a licensing decision, with no subscriber count, price or coverage figure published ([reseller](2026-08-25-developingtelecoms-paratus-uganda-starlink-launch)).

Partner states opened a joint funding account for a regional communications satellite study with deposits due 30 September 2026, and neither the study's cost nor each state's share was disclosed ([satellite](2026-08-24-chimpreports-ncip-partner-state-communications-satellite-study)).

2026-09-02 — the operator began commercial service, ending the regulatory process that followed a memorandum and a five-year licence signed with the regulator in May 2026. The licence requires a national gateway and physical point of presence, an operational office and registration of every device activated in the country, conditions the regulator framed as security, revenue assurance, accountability and compliance with Ugandan law ([launch](2026-09-02-newvision-starlink-launch-uganda), [pricing](2026-09-02-starlink-launches-uganda-pricing)). The January wholesale ruling and the May direct licence remain unreconciled on the record.

summary: The [universal service fund](2026-08-03-atc-uganda-contributes-ugx-20-9bn-to-support-universal-access) retains half the statutory levy with no balance published, and the [six-year rural inclusion programme closed reporting 3.4m registered users but only about 29 per cent active](2026-08-26-uncdf-connect-rural-uganda-sida-lnob-closeout-review).
developments:
An operator remitted UGX 20.9bn at a handover ceremony; half the statutory 2 per cent levy goes to the consolidated fund and only half is retained, no fund balance or annual total is published, and the statutory basis is a named section of the 2013 communications Act ([fund](2026-08-03-atc-uganda-contributes-ugx-20-9bn-to-support-universal-access), [contribution](2026-08-05-atc-uganda-ucusaf-contribution), [remittance](2026-07-31-uganda-atc-contributes-universal-service-fund-ucusaf)).

The foreign agency's withdrawal cut 83 per cent of its programmes ([withdrawal](2026-08-12-usaid-exit-connectivity-gap-africa)); a multi-funder digital-economy fund lost its American component while the parts other funders backed continued, and no figure for the national share is stated ([withdrawal](2026-08-12-usaid-exit-connectivity-gap-africa)).

Border free public wireless access was launched two weeks before the window opened ([border](2025-07-14-free-wifi-uganda-drc-border-nita)).

The US$15m Swedish-funded rural inclusion programme closed on a 2019-2025 term, and its close-out is the only outcome record held for it: more than 3.4 million registered users of whom about 29 per cent were active, more than 21,000 agents recruited, 26 services piloted, and its own statement that technology alone could not close the usage gap ([close-out](2026-08-26-uncdf-connect-rural-uganda-sida-lnob-closeout-review), [closure](2026-08-27-pulse-uganda-uncdf-digital-inclusion-closeout)). No successor is on file, and registration counts what a programme reached, not what it changed.

summary: A [colocation facility operates outside the capital](2026-07-15 Raxio data-centre capital tops $380m on investor boost), a [green tier-three build slipped to early 2026](2025-10-03 Centenary Group set to launch its Green Tier 3 Data Centre in 2026), and an [edge site](2024-12-13 Nxtra - Airtel's leap into Africa's growing data center market) is named with no date or capacity.
developments:
The colocation facility's capital figure is group-level across seven markets, not national ([colocation](2026-07-15 Raxio data-centre capital tops $380m on investor boost), [stack](2024-08-12 Liquid Intelligent Technologies launches Azure Stack in Uganda)).

The green build was rebased from late 2025 to the first quarter of 2026, and the slip is visible only across two clips from one publisher ([rebase](2025-10-03 Centenary Group set to launch its Green Tier 3 Data Centre in 2026), [original](2025-08-11 Centenary Group affirms data centre will be ready by late 2025)).

The edge site is named as a future site with no date or capacity attached ([edge](2024-12-13 Nxtra - Airtel's leap into Africa's growing data center market)). No national capacity figure appears anywhere in this ledger.

summary: A [domestic sovereign cloud](2026-03-02 ABQ Cloud launches Ugandan sovereign cloud ecosystem) launched at a commercial facility, and a [national artificial-intelligence research cloud](2026-03-16-musenero-launches-national-ai-research-cloud) launched at the national university framed as replacing foreign cloud on sovereignty grounds.
developments:
The sovereign cloud is domestically owned and the building is a commercial operator's ([cloud](2026-03-02 ABQ Cloud launches Ugandan sovereign cloud ecosystem)).

The research cloud launched in March 2026 with the national research and education network, framed as replacing foreign cloud on data-sovereignty grounds ([research cloud](2026-03-16-musenero-launches-national-ai-research-cloud)).

Neither publishes capacity, tenancy or utilisation. Sovereignty framing applied to a service running in someone else's building is the distinction worth keeping.

summary: A [supercomputer centre at a hydropower plant](2026-01-28 Uganda to Launch Africa's First Home-Grown AI Supercomputer Center at Karuma Hydropower Plant) is stated to begin rollout in 2026 at full capacity in 2028, on a single-sourced cost with a contested first-in-Africa label the base adopts neither of.
developments:
The rollout claim and the US$1.2bn cost are single-sourced, and the first-in-Africa label is contested ([centre](2026-01-28 Uganda to Launch Africa's First Home-Grown AI Supercomputer Center at Karuma Hydropower Plant), [build](2025-09-15 Synectics, Schneider to build AI center in Uganda starting 2026)).

The surplus-power case is a promoter's design claim tied to that rollout, with no grid-operator or generator confirmation held ([power](2025-09-15 Synectics, Schneider to build AI center in Uganda starting 2026)).

Siting compute at a generator is the one energy argument in this unit with a physical basis, and it rests entirely on the promoter's own account.

summary: The leading operator reports a [share of network sites on solar or hydro](2026-08-05-mtn-uganda-sustainability-report-2025) in its 2025 sustainability report, on its own unaudited figure with no prior-year share held.
developments:
It is the company's own unaudited figure for the year to December 2025 ([sites](2026-08-05-mtn-uganda-sustainability-report-2025)).

It is the only energy measure attached to network operation in this ledger, and no regulator or grid series accompanies it.

summary: A [National Information Security Framework 2026](2026-07-16-uganda-updated-national-information-security-framework) was launched under the donor project with the document itself not held, and [cyberattack volume](2026-07-16-uganda-updated-national-information-security-framework) was cited at the launch with base period and absolute counts unpublished.
developments:
The framework was launched by the ICT ministry in July 2026 and the document is not held ([framework](2026-07-16-uganda-updated-national-information-security-framework)).

The attack-volume figure was cited at that launch without a base period or absolute counts ([volume](2026-07-16-uganda-updated-national-information-security-framework)), and the only recorded cybercrime case figure is a police count for calendar 2024, with both ends predating the progress window ([cases](2026-01-30-experts-urge-tougher-cybersecurity-financial-sector)).

An anti-piracy coordination framework is exploring dynamic address and name-system blocking, and participants flagged the dual use of blocking infrastructure built for piracy ([piracy](2026-07-17-ucc-national-push-against-digital-piracy)) — which is the same infrastructure question the election-period suspension raises. Legitimate pay-television subscriptions fell on the figure cited at that convening ([subscriptions](2026-07-17-ucc-national-push-against-digital-piracy)).

The criminal investigations directorate told a parliamentary committee inspection that its Crime Data Centre, originally due earlier, is now targeted for March 2027, that it will recruit internally to close an investigator shortage, and that it wants government and security databases integrated so detectives can link suspects, incidents and evidence quickly - integration its director said would first require agreement on the legal and policy frameworks governing access ([directorate](2026-08-27-nilepost-cid-digital-crime-investigators)).

progress: Mixed, 28.5m legacy records migrated to a new platform while the new cards' machine-readable codes do not work
summary: [28,571,893 legacy records were migrated](2026-02-11 Uganda migrates more than 28M records to new national ID system) in the platform's first brownfield migration, while the [enhanced card machine-readable code does not work](2026-08-20-parliament-uganda-new-id-system-questions-digital-verification) and has not since at least February 2026.
developments:
The migration completed with about 200,000 duplicates found over seven months ([migration](2026-02-11 Uganda migrates more than 28M records to new national ID system), [brownfield](2026-02-19-mosip-brownfield-sierra-leone-migration), [renewals](2025-07-16-5m-ugandans-renew-national-ids), [modules](2025-04-14-uganda-launching-5-mosip-modules)).

The code failure was raised in Parliament in August 2026 and has stood since at least February with no published fix date and no count of affected cards. Parliament's own record has the registration authority acknowledging in February that the functionality had not been integrated into its digital operational system and promising a fix by 31 March ([failure](2026-08-20-parliament-uganda-new-id-system-questions-digital-verification), [codes](2026-08-21-techbuild-uganda-national-id-broken-qr-codes), [problems](2026-08-19-kampalapress-ndaga-muntu-new-national-ids-problems)).

A register data-breach investigation was opened with the protection office and police in September 2025 with no outcome, and a civil-society body demanded a fully independent inquiry ([breach](2025-09-22-nira-tighten-id-security-after-breach)).

summary: Over [60 per cent of printed cards are uncollected](2026-02-09-35-million-registered-national-id-milestone), and the [auditor general recorded a backlog](2026-08-11-uganda-nira-id-nightmare-queues-auditor-general) whose figures were ten months old at publication with no current series published.
developments:
The identification authority holds 36.15 million people on the national register, close to 77% of the population ([figure](2026-09-01-newvision-uganda-nira-register-36m)).

The mass exercise closed in February 2026 with over 60 per cent of printed cards uncollected ([printed](2026-02-09-35-million-registered-national-id-milestone), [renewals](2025-07-16-5m-ugandans-renew-national-ids)).

The auditor's figures are as at late October 2025 and are reported alongside cross-district queue chaos over new-card collection; the authority publishes no current backlog series ([backlog](2026-08-11-uganda-nira-id-nightmare-queues-auditor-general)).

First-time enrolment against target and renewal ran at two different rates, and the two rates are the finding: efficient for people already on the register ([enrolment](2026-02-11 Uganda migrates more than 28M records to new national ID system)). A further mass drive was stated to Parliament with no start date, budget or delivery plan on record ([drive](2026-08-20-parliament-uganda-new-id-system-questions-digital-verification)).

summary: [Iris hardware was deployed on more than 5,665 registration kits](2026-03-02 IriTech provides iris biometrics for Uganda's upgraded registration kits), the [authority establishment was expanded](2026-08-20-parliament-uganda-new-id-system-questions-digital-verification), and the [system contract](2026-02-11 Uganda migrates more than 28M records to new national ID system) is single-sourced with no value, award date or term held.
developments:
The iris deployment covers the 2024 to 2026 campaign; the registry figures are vendor-sourced and two roughly one-million populations are distinct and must not be summed ([iris](2026-03-02 IriTech provides iris biometrics for Uganda's upgraded registration kits), [unmatched](2024-07-02-nira-iris-scanning-1m-unmatched-fingerprints-ubc)).

The establishment expansion was stated in plenary in August 2026; it is an establishment figure rather than a filled-post figure, with no recruitment timetable or wage provision stated ([establishment](2026-08-20-parliament-uganda-new-id-system-questions-digital-verification), [support](2026-08-07-uganda-minister-kamuntu-pledges-government-support-to-strengthen-nira)).

The contract behind the migration is single-sourced with no contract value, award date or term held, and it is the whole of that relationship in this base ([contract](2026-02-11 Uganda migrates more than 28M records to new national ID system)).

summary: [Seventy-four financial institutions](2024-10-14 Uganda financial institutions sign on for digital KYC through national ID) had electronic verification access to the register as at June 2024, and a [constitutional challenge to identity-based access](2025-06-10-iser-v-attorney-general-nira-uganda-digital-id-ruling) was dismissed with each party bearing its own costs.
developments:
The institution count reaches the base through a central-bank annual report that is not itself held ([institutions](2024-10-14 Uganda financial institutions sign on for digital KYC through national ID)).

The challenge was dismissed in June 2025; the case number is a specific miscellaneous cause, not the form circulated in secondary coverage ([ruling](2025-06-10-iser-v-attorney-general-nira-uganda-digital-id-ruling), [barrier](2025-09-13 Uganda's Digital ID Barrier Worsens as Court Delivers Blow to Access)).

A dismissed challenge, a two-year-old institution count and a machine-readable code that does not work are the three things this base can say about the credential's use.

summary: [First alien identity cards were issued](2026-08-20-nilepost-nira-alien-id-foreign-nationals) with 1,875 enrolled in ten weeks, against a scope of which about 1.95m are refugees or asylum-seekers, and a US$100 fee.
developments:
Enrolment of 1,875 in ten weeks is under a tenth of a per cent of the scope, and the fee falls on a population overwhelmingly composed of refugees ([cards](2026-08-20-nilepost-nira-alien-id-foreign-nationals), [registration](2026-06-04-nira-first-registration-of-foreigners), [births](2026-06-01-nira-birth-registration-alien-registration)).

Nothing is published about a waiver, an instalment route, or what happens to a resident foreigner who cannot pay yet needs a subscriber card or a bank account.

That combination — a fee at that level, on that population, with no waiver published — is the sharpest exclusion finding in this unit.

summary: A [birth registration drive](2026-06-01-nira-birth-registration-alien-registration) announced community drives and a fee schedule, and no birth-registration coverage figure has been published since 2016.
developments:
The drive and fee schedule were announced in June 2026 ([drive](2026-06-01-nira-birth-registration-alien-registration), [notification](2020-01-01 Maintaining civil registration amid COVID-19 - Uganda's mobile notification system (IDRC))).

Ten years without a published coverage figure means the drive cannot be measured against anything.

Marriage registration transferred from the registration bureau to the identity authority in April 2025, three months before the window opened ([marriage](2025-04-25-ursb-hands-marriage-registration-to-nira)).

summary: A [non-individual register](2026-05-08-ursb-non-individual-register-launch) launched in May 2026 as the corporate counterpart to the national identity number, with no registered-entity count published.
developments:
It launched in May 2026 ([register](2026-05-08-ursb-non-individual-register-launch)).

Giving legal persons an identifier matching the one natural persons hold is the design that lets the two be joined, and no source states whether they are.

summary: [Land registry digitisation](2026-04-07-govt-tightens-land-controls-blockchain-ai) is a lands ministry statement of intent, with an administrative circular the operative instrument and the technology intent only.
developments:
The statement was reported in April 2026, mentioning distributed ledgers and artificial intelligence ([intent](2026-04-07-govt-tightens-land-controls-blockchain-ai)).

The operative instrument is an administrative circular of 2025; the technology is intent only. Distinguishing the circular from the technology talk is the whole of what can be said here.

progress: Mixed, cash-withdrawal caps set for 2027 while the payment switch and the settlement-system replacement both stand unmoved
summary: [Cash-withdrawal caps](2026-06-03-bou-cash-withdrawal-limits-cash-lite) take effect on 1 January 2027 for a cash-lite economy, while the [national payment switch](2025-10-06 BoU's New Payment System Cuts Delays and Boosts E-Money by 28.6%) and the [settlement-system replacement](2025-10-06 BoU's New Payment System Cuts Delays and Boosts E-Money by 28.6%) are unmoved.
developments:
The caps were issued by circular in May 2026 for a January 2027 start, the stated purpose being a cash-lite economy ([caps](2026-06-03-bou-cash-withdrawal-limits-cash-lite)).

The switch was reported in progress in the central bank's 2024/25 account and has not moved ([switch](2025-10-06 BoU's New Payment System Cuts Delays and Boosts E-Money by 28.6%)). The settlement replacement and standards migration had a stated go-live of November 2025 which passed unverified; absence of confirmation is not evidence of non-delivery ([settlement](2025-10-06 BoU's New Payment System Cuts Delays and Boosts E-Money by 28.6%)).

A digital shilling pilot was announced inside a US$5.5bn settlement-network plan in October 2025 with nothing since ([pilot](2025-10-08-uganda-5-5bn-digital-project-cbdc-shilling)). Capping cash before the rail that would replace it is confirmed working is the sequence.

summary: [Electronic money transaction value grew 28.6 per cent](2025-10-06 BoU's New Payment System Cuts Delays and Boosts E-Money by 28.6%) with growth in agents and handsets while both screen-based channels contracted, and [active wallet users](2026-08-05-mtn-uganda-sustainability-report-2025) rose on the operator's own report.
developments:
The growth sits in agents and handsets; both screen-based channels contracted ([value](2025-10-06 BoU's New Payment System Cuts Delays and Boosts E-Money by 28.6%)).

The operator's two transaction-value figures are not reconcilable and no growth rate is derived from them ([users](2026-08-05-mtn-uganda-sustainability-report-2025), [separation](2025-07-23-mtn-uganda-shareholders-approve-momo-separation)).

Shareholders approved separating the money business into a new financial company in July 2025 ([spin-off](2025-07-23-mtn-uganda-shareholders-approve-momo-separation)), and the platform migrated to a cloud-native vendor platform across four markets on the vendor's own performance figures ([migration](2026-08-21-tan-ericsson-mtn-momo-cloud-migration)).

summary: [One commercial bank went live on the continental payment rail](2026-08-03-papss-uba-uganda-joins), [direct yuan settlement opened](2026-08-07-uganda-stanbic-china-cips-yuan-payments) through one bank, and a [stablecoin settlement corridor](2026-07-16-scrypt-stablecoin-settlement-uganda-corridor) opened.
developments:
A single commercial bank's subsidiary announced going live on the continental rail in August 2026 ([rail](2026-08-03-papss-uba-uganda-joins)).

Direct yuan settlement opened for domestic businesses through one bank's service rather than a national rail, with no volume, fee or central-bank position stated ([yuan](2026-08-07-uganda-stanbic-china-cips-yuan-payments)).

A stablecoin settlement corridor opened in July 2026 ([stablecoin](2026-07-16-scrypt-stablecoin-settlement-uganda-corridor)), and card acceptance was extended to nine African markets with merchant and card counts given as the two companies' own and no country-specific figure ([cards](2026-08-19-tan-unionpay-standard-bank-nine-african-markets)). Four cross-border arrangements, none of them a national rail.

summary: A [wallet insurance distribution product](2026-07-22-airtel-money-uganda-britam-insurance) went live, a [tokenised-asset exchange](2026-04-08-gsh-acquire-akiba-tokenised-capital-markets) changed hands, and a [bank and platform memorandum](2026-07-24-uganda-centenary-micropay-partner-digital-access-education-healthcare-insurance) carries a credit-scoring layer with nothing on file about consent, retention or legal basis.
developments:
The insurance product's first offering went live in July 2026 with no premium, policy-count or target published ([insurance](2026-07-22-airtel-money-uganda-britam-insurance)).

A majority stake in the tokenised-asset exchange moved in April 2026 ([exchange](2026-04-08-gsh-acquire-akiba-tokenised-capital-markets)).

The bank and platform memorandum's signature date is unestablished, and nothing is on file about consent, retention or legal basis for the credit-scoring layer ([memorandum](2026-07-24-uganda-centenary-micropay-partner-digital-access-education-healthcare-insurance)). A short-code micro-investing pilot reaches the base only as a comparator in a foreign-led survey, with no domestic source, provider name or launch date held ([pilot](2026-07-31-vodacom-lesotho-brings-micro-investing-to-m-pesa)).

summary: A [National Financial Inclusion Strategy 2023-2028](2023-11-01 Uganda National Financial Inclusion Strategy 2023-2028 (NFIS II)) was published in November 2023 and nothing in the base moves it.
developments:
It was published in November 2023 ([strategy](2023-11-01 Uganda National Financial Inclusion Strategy 2023-2028 (NFIS II))).

No mid-term review, target position or consumer-protection instrument under it appears anywhere in this ledger, against a payments record that includes a stablecoin corridor, a tokenised exchange, buy-now-pay-later device credit with no published default figure, and digital lending regulation that exists only as a stated intention.

summary: [Mandatory electronic invoicing](2026-08-19-horn-uganda-kenya-electronic-invoicing-divergence) was phased in by revenue-authority notice, the [tax identification number is to merge into the national identity number](2025-11-11 URA Launches Tax Filing Season, Announces Shift from TIN to NIN), and an [electronic tax software award](2026-07-29-uganda-ura-electronic-tax-software-e-tax2-procurement-scandal) has no work started and no performance guarantee.
developments:
The invoicing rollout was mandated by a public notice of August 2026 which is not held; the account is a regional trade publication's and no compliance figures or penalties are stated ([invoicing](2026-08-19-horn-uganda-kenya-electronic-invoicing-divergence)).

The identifier merger was announced under a tax procedures amendment bill in November 2025 ([merger](2025-11-11 URA Launches Tax Filing Season, Announces Shift from TIN to NIN), [shift](2025-11-12-ura-shift-from-tin-to-nin)), and tax payment on the leading wallet launched in December 2025 with the stated rationale of making informal activity visible for the tax net ([wallet tax](2025-12-23 URA Launches Enhanced Tax Payment Services on MTN MoMo to Boost Digital Compliance)).

The software award had no work started as at July 2026 and no performance guarantee issued; the contract and evaluation report are not held and press allegations are recorded as allegations ([award](2026-07-29-uganda-ura-electronic-tax-software-e-tax2-procurement-scandal), [tribunal](2025-10-03-ppda-appeals-tribunal-yoya-aisino-vs-ura-etax-decision)).

summary: A [national laboratory data repository](2026-02-05-national-laboratory-data-repository-health) launched in February 2026 extending the existing health-information stack, and the [health management information system](2025-12-01-impulse-erhis-newborn-data-functionalities) was assessed only through a cross-sectional study.
developments:
The repository launched in February 2026 and extends the existing stack ([repository](2026-02-05-national-laboratory-data-repository-health)).

The management information system's newborn-data functionality was assessed across 53 data offices in four countries in a study run between November 2022 and July 2024; no national coverage or maturity figure is held ([assessment](2025-12-01-impulse-erhis-newborn-data-functionalities)).

Health data is also the subject of the bilateral arrangement recorded separately, whose data-sharing agreement is still to be executed.

summary: A [human rights commission case-management system](2026-08-12-uganda-launches-two-new-e-services-to-digitise-teacher-training-human-rights-cas) was launched in August 2026 under the government network programme.
developments:
It was launched alongside a teacher-training platform under the same programme ([system](2026-08-12-uganda-launches-two-new-e-services-to-digitise-teacher-training-human-rights-cas)).

No case volume, complaint route or public-access provision is published. It sits alongside the judiciary's case-management system, through which revised media guidelines were issued for a High Court trial — the same infrastructure serving both a rights body and a restriction on reporting.

summary: [Electronic government procurement training opened for 100 further entities](2026-08-03-accounting-officers-trained-as-uganda-expands-electronic-procurement-system) with onboarding to continue each financial year, and a [copyright management system](2026-08-20-nilepost-copyright-management-system-rollout) targets a September 2026 rollout.
developments:
The procurement start figure carries no date, and the authority states onboarding continues each financial year until all of government is on the system ([procurement](2026-08-03-accounting-officers-trained-as-uganda-expands-electronic-procurement-system)).

A procurement portal upgrade to an infrastructure data standard was announced in November 2025 ([portal](2025-11-14-govt-upgrade-procurement-portal-oc4ids)).

The copyright system is in testing with a September 2026 target; no cost, supplier, rights-holder count or description of what it registers or pays out is published, and the target date is the only dated commitment held ([copyright](2026-08-20-nilepost-copyright-management-system-rollout)). A teacher-training platform launched in August 2026 ([teachers](2026-08-12-uganda-launches-two-new-e-services-to-digitise-teacher-training-human-rights-cas)).

summary: [Six of nineteen service centres](2026-07-27-uganda-tororo-one-stop-service-uganda-centre-inspection) were operational at a readiness inspection, and the two accounts conflict on the early-2026 operational count.
developments:
Six of nineteen were operational at the inspection, and two accounts conflict on the early-2026 count ([centres](2026-07-27-uganda-tororo-one-stop-service-uganda-centre-inspection), [construction](2026-03-13-service-uganda-centre-construction-gulu)).

A further centre began construction on a USh4bn contract at the postal service's premises, on a model cabinet approved in 2019 ([centre](2026-03-13-service-uganda-centre-construction-gulu)).

Their throughput was made contingent on a backbone phase whose latest reported position is a 2023 loan approval, so the constraint on the one-stop centres sits outside the centre programme.

summary: [Open-source language models for African languages](2025-10-10-sunbird-ai-sunflower-african-languages-medium) were released under a permissive licence, and the developer records unreliable factual recall and weak handling of informal language.
developments:
They were released in October 2025 by a not-for-profit developer with the national university; the benchmark claim is its own, and it records unreliable factual recall and weak handling of informal language ([models](2025-10-10-sunbird-ai-sunflower-african-languages-medium), [coverage](2025-10-08-sunflower-expanding-coverage-african-languages-llms-arxiv)).

A wire report of another outlet's reporting states a later model was built on a Chinese open-weight base; no user count, licence terms or evaluation is held, and the same report puts Chinese open-weight models at 17.1 per cent of global downloads against 15.8 for American ones over the year ([base model](2026-08-07-asiae-chinese-open-source-ai-africa-developers)).

A developer publishing its own model's weaknesses is unusual and worth recording as such.

summary: A [directive on artificial intelligence in medical curricula](2026-08-12-uganda-medical-schools-ai-integration-training) was issued to training schools with no curriculum standard, syllabus, teaching capacity assessment or funding attached.
developments:
The directive was issued in August 2026 ([directive](2026-08-12-uganda-medical-schools-ai-integration-training)).

Directing every medical training school to teach a subject, with no standard, syllabus, capacity assessment or funding, is the whole of the record. The national strategy that would frame it has been due by the financial year's end at both ends of the window.

summary: An [operator completed a US$63m acquisition](2025-11-11 YAS completes $63m acquisition of parent company of Zuku and Simbanet) of a regional connectivity group's parent, all regulatory approvals cleared.
developments:
Completion was announced in the capital in November 2025 ([acquisition](2025-11-11 YAS completes $63m acquisition of parent company of Zuku and Simbanet)).

It is the only market-structure transaction in this ledger, and no regulator statement, condition or market-share analysis accompanies it.

summary: [Four regional innovation hubs](2026-08-04-ministry-reviews-5-year-performance-on-ugandas-digital-transformation-journey) were stated operational on the ministry's own count, and a [bilateral memorandum](2026-02-20-mbale-ict-hub-uk-mou-women-skills) builds on two centres that graduated 800 young women with 60 per cent reported employed.
developments:
The four-hub count is the ministry's own with no user, cohort or budget figure published and the review report not on file ([hubs](2026-08-04-ministry-reviews-5-year-performance-on-ugandas-digital-transformation-journey)).

The bilateral memorandum was signed in February 2026 and builds on two existing centres that graduated 800 young women, 60 per cent of them reported employed ([memorandum](2026-02-20-mbale-ict-hub-uk-mou-women-skills)).

A fintech forum was launched by the national university's incubation centre with a private partner; it is a forum, not a finance instrument ([forum](2026-07-13-makerere-afriventia-fintech-fridays)).

summary: A [national innovator registry](2026-05-19-govt-turns-to-local-innovators-national-innovator-registry) excludes joint ventures with foreign firms and confers no contract, and a [three-year startup income-tax exemption](2025-04-02-uganda-startup-income-tax-exemption) was proposed with no enactment recorded.
developments:
The registry's gazettement was scheduled for July 2026 with no confirmation held; it excludes joint ventures with foreign firms and enrolment confers no contract ([registry](2026-05-19-govt-turns-to-local-innovators-national-innovator-registry), [prototype](2026-05-22 Uganda launches prototype program for digital ID and public infrastructure)).

The tax exemption was proposed in 2025 income tax bill amendments with no enactment recorded, and is distinct from a small-capital exemption in force from July 2025 ([exemption](2025-04-02-uganda-startup-income-tax-exemption)).

Startups raising disclosed funding are counted by a publisher from disclosed rounds only and are not comparable with the investment series ([funding](2026-02-03-disrupt-africa-african-tech-startups-funding-report-2025)), and a diversity study samples more than 3,000 startups with no prior national figure held ([diversity](2026-08-04-diversity-dividend-female-startup-cofounders)).

2026-08-31 — a continental alliance and the ICT ministry [validated a national digital entrepreneurship and innovation assessment at a Kampala workshop, which named as priorities advancing the Startup Bill, strengthening science, technology and innovation policy, widening access to regulatory sandboxes and using public procurement to open markets to local startups](2026-08-31-techafricanews-smart-africa-uganda-reforms). The assessment text is not published and no reform is dated or budgeted; the Startup Bill itself is carried on this ledger as not held, the base holding no text, stage or timetable for it.

summary: A [rider digital skilling programme](2025-11-17-ucc-market-performance-report-q3-2025) onboarded 3,000 riders in one quarter of 2025 and the base holds no later quarterly, and [digital skilling for faith-based health centres](2026-08-19-newvision-ucc-digital-skilling-health-centres) launched in August 2026.
developments:
The rider figure is the window-opening quarter carried forward unrefreshed, the base holding no later quarterly report ([riders](2025-11-17-ucc-market-performance-report-q3-2025)).

The health-centre programme launched in August 2026 ([health centres](2026-08-19-newvision-ucc-digital-skilling-health-centres)).

Neither carries a curriculum, completion measure or follow-up, and one is a single quarter of a series the base cannot continue.

summary: A [three-day course on digital crime and evidence](2026-08-20-nilepost-judiciary-digital-crime-ict-training) opened for judges and magistrates, with more than 100 prosecuted communications offences since 2018 behind it.
developments:
No cohort size, curriculum or repeat schedule is published, so whether it reaches the bench as a whole or a single sitting of it is not stated ([course](2026-08-20-nilepost-judiciary-digital-crime-ict-training)).

It matters because the Constitutional Court has just nullified five sections of the principal computer-crime statute, and the offences that remain will be tried by the judges this course reaches or misses.

summary: The technology institute reports [more than 48,000 trained](2026-08-07-uict-trains-more-than-48000-ugandans-in-digital-and-emerging-technologies) in one financial year, self-reported and unaudited, with fewer than 4 per cent of them government officers.
developments:
The figures are the institute's own, reported to a sector performance review ([output](2026-08-07-uict-trains-more-than-48000-ugandans-in-digital-and-emerging-technologies)).

Fewer than 4 per cent of those trained were government officers ([officers](2026-08-07-uict-trains-more-than-48000-ugandans-in-digital-and-emerging-technologies)), which is the finding rather than the headline count: the state's own training institute is largely not training the state.

An inclusive artificial-intelligence curriculum was reported under development at the same institute, paired with a roadmap goal of functional innovation hubs in every region by 2027 ([curriculum](2025-11-18-govt-inclusive-ai-curriculum-learners)).

summary: An [inventory of commercialisable software](2026-07-31-govt-moves-to-commercialise-homegrown-digital-innovations) was ordered on a two-week deadline, and an [entrepreneurship programme](2026-07-22-uict-uj-connect-batch-four) launched its final cohort.
developments:
The inventory addresses a past-pilot scale gap named by an operator in June 2026 ([inventory](2026-07-31-govt-moves-to-commercialise-homegrown-digital-innovations), [commercialisation](2026-08-03-uganda-ict-ministry-uict-commercialisation)).

The entrepreneurship programme's fourth batch is the project's final cohort, and the institute states entrepreneurship becomes a standing pillar after the project closes ([batch](2026-07-22-uict-uj-connect-batch-four), [innovators](2026-07-31-ouganda-83-innovateurs-programme-entrepreneuriat)).

A US$200m skills commitment running to 2030 is the largest single skills commitment in the tracked non-state set ([commitment](2020-01-01-mcf-uga-youngafricaworks-2020-young-africa-works-in-uganda)).

2026-08-31 — an operator's skilling programme [graduated 503 young people in its 2026 cohort at the National ICT Innovation Hub, in a hybrid course covering ICT, digital marketing, e-commerce, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence, taking its cumulative total to 1,191](2026-08-31-techafricanews-mtn-uganda-digital-skills). The counts are the operator's own, and no employment outcome, start year or cost per participant is published.

summary: An [ICT hub for persons with disabilities](2026-08-01-new-ict-hub-in-kasese-to-empower-persons-with-disabilities-with-digital-skills) was commissioned in August 2026 with no commitment value published, and [information technology training for youth with disabilities](2025-01-01-iati-xm-dac-21-1-2025000869b2miscara-it-training-youth-with-disabilities-uganda) recorded a disbursement for 2025.
developments:
The hub was commissioned with no commitment value published, so the base carries no finance record for it ([hub](2026-08-01-new-ict-hub-in-kasese-to-empower-persons-with-disabilities-with-digital-skills), [commissioning](2026-08-03-koica-ict-hub-kasese-persons-with-disabilities)).

The training record is a commitment rather than a delivery report, with no trainee count, curriculum or outcome stated ([training](2025-01-01-iati-xm-dac-21-1-2025000869b2miscara-it-training-youth-with-disabilities-uganda)).

Two disability-specific instruments, neither with a published outcome, is more than most units in this frame hold and still not a measurable programme.

summary: A [EUR 2,250,000 girls and women digital programme](2021-01-01-enabel-uga-d4gw-2021-digital-for-girls-and-women-uganda) ran 2021 to 2025 and its stated period has elapsed — the only gender-and-digital-skills commitment in the tracked non-state set.
developments:
The commitment is recorded for 2021 to 2025 and the period has elapsed ([programme](2021-01-01-enabel-uga-d4gw-2021-digital-for-girls-and-women-uganda)).

No successor is held. A diversity study of female startup co-founders is the only other gender measure in this ledger, and it holds no prior national figure to compare against.

summary: A secretariat review of [quarterly performance submissions](2026-07-30-uganda-pstp-secretariat-performance-reporting-quality-mdas) found reporting quality wanting — the government's own statement about its central performance-data pipeline.
developments:
The review covered 2025/26 submissions under the fourth national development plan ([review](2026-07-30-uganda-pstp-secretariat-performance-reporting-quality-mdas)).

It is the government's own statement about its own pipeline, which is what gives it weight.

A labour, employment and productivity reporting programme was launched in June 2026 with no budget, system name or delivery date ([labour](2026-06-15-gender-ministry-labour-market-data-programme)).

summary: [Eighty data collectors were commissioned](2026-08-04-ubos-commissions-80-data-collectors-for-9th-uganda-national-household-survey) for twelve months of collection on the ninth national household survey, with no sample size, budget, funder or publication date stated.
developments:
The collectors were commissioned in August 2026 ([survey](2026-08-04-ubos-commissions-80-data-collectors-for-9th-uganda-national-household-survey)).

A statistics office block broke ground in August 2026; government states it is fully financed domestically but publishes no figure, so no finance record is built, and a bid to host the regional statistics bureau is a pledge to engage partner states rather than a confirmed award ([block](2026-08-07-uganda-ubos-statistics-house-groundbreaking), [bid](2026-08-16-observer-uganda-east-african-statistics-bureau-bid)).

A twelve-month household survey with no published sample design is the instrument every population-denominated figure in this report will eventually rest on.

summary: A [mapping report on procurement portal conformance](2025-11-14-govt-upgrade-procurement-portal-oc4ids) with an infrastructure data standard was presented, and no delivery record has followed.
developments:
The authority committed to reflecting the data points in a coming upgrade; no delivery record since ([mapping](2025-11-14-govt-upgrade-procurement-portal-oc4ids)).

It is the only open-data item in this ledger. No national open-data portal, catalogue or policy appears anywhere in it.

progress: Mixed, a signed health memorandum providing only for a future agreement while an investigation describes direct real-time access to nine systems
summary: A [United States health-data access agreement](2026-08-19-senators-criticize-us-demands-for-foreign-health-data) was signed in December 2025 for activities to 2030, and two accounts describe different instruments rather than a conflict.
developments:
The signed memorandum is held and only provides for a future data sharing agreement at a numbered clause; a published investigation says it reviewed that agreement directly and describes direct, real-time access to nine systems for seven years. The two accounts describe different instruments, not a conflict ([agreement](2026-08-19-senators-criticize-us-demands-for-foreign-health-data), [memorandum](2025-12-10-afghs-mou-uganda), [record](2025-12-10-state-uga-afghs-data-systems-2025-record), [investigation](2026-07-23-propublica-us-health-data-agreements-africa-digital-colonialism)).

Distinguishing the memorandum from the agreement it provides for is the whole of the reconciliation, and it is what stops this reading as either a denial or an exposé.

summary: A [banking partnership](2026-05-23-huawei-centenary-bank-digital-partnership) covering eight areas was signed in Shanghai, and an [artificial-intelligence skills memorandum](2026-04-01-ict-ministry-mou-un-health-china-ai-skills) carries jobs and economy figures that are the partner chairman's projections.
developments:
The banking agreement is company-reported with no contract value, duration or delivery milestone published ([banking](2026-05-23-huawei-centenary-bank-digital-partnership)).

The skills memorandum was signed with a United Nations health industry foundation and a private foundation; the 50,000 jobs and the 2040 economy figure are the partner chairman's projections, not commitments ([skills](2026-04-01-ict-ministry-mou-un-health-china-ai-skills)).

The country's own open-source language model is separately reported as built on a Chinese open-weight base, which is the substantive dependency rather than either memorandum.

summary: A [regional infrastructure acceleration technical assistance tender](2026-07-31-giz-bmz-eac-dpi-technical-assistance-tender) was published with requests to participate due September 2026, and a [national funding window for a sovereign infrastructure loan package](2026-07-31-giz-bmz-eac-dpi-technical-assistance-tender) was named within it.
developments:
The tender was published in July 2026 ([tender](2026-07-31-giz-bmz-eac-dpi-technical-assistance-tender)), and the delegation's funding is named as an added national window inside it ([window](2026-07-31-giz-bmz-eac-dpi-technical-assistance-tender)).

A separate regional project pipeline consultancy was tendered in August 2026 under the same programme; the record is a procurement notice, so it fixes the consultancy stage and nothing about any project it may prepare ([pipeline](2026-08-05-eac-dpi-consulting-ostafrika-giz-bmz-tender)).

Three procurement notices and no financed project is the state of the European relationship on this record.

summary: Expressway tolls are [still collected in cash](2026-08-26-newvision-ura-toll-collection-expressway), with a parliamentary committee recommending a revenue-authority takeover and an electronic payment system.
developments: The Kampala-Entebbe Expressway concession remains reliant on cash. A parliamentary infrastructure committee recommended on 25 August 2026 that the revenue authority take over collection and introduce an electronic payment system, called for a forensic audit of the concession's operations and revenue collections, and asked for scrutiny of a reported UGX 36 billion contract extension; the ICT minister of state told the House that the operator has never given government the source code or password of the system ([committee](2026-08-26-newvision-ura-toll-collection-expressway)).

summary: Cabinet approved that the national identification number will replace the taxpayer identification number in all transactions ([report](2026-09-01-businesstimesug-uganda-nin-replace-tin)).
developments: Cabinet approved that the national identification number will replace the taxpayer identification number in all transactions ([report](2026-09-01-businesstimesug-uganda-nin-replace-tin)). No commencement date or transition arrangement is stated, and a register that reaches 77% of the population is the base it would run on.
